turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you again, Sandip, for your sake as well as for the sake of your followers. I will not tolerate any further oppression of my tenantry.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And if you think you can protect them from me, Nikhil, how many men do you have, and how many have I? I'd wager my estates against yours that I can outlast you in this petty game of threats.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am not concerned with the number of men at our disposal, Sandip. What I am concerned with is the well-being of my people, and I will take whatever measures are necessary to ensure their safety.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what of your precious Mussulman allies, Nikhil? I'm sure they're just as eager to see me beg for mercy as you are.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I have made it clear, Sandip, that I will not stand idly by while you continue to exploit and oppress our mutual tenantry.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, so now you're playing the hero, Nikhil? How quaint. I'm shaking in my boots at the thought of your righteous indignation.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I warn you, Sandip, for the last time: cease your provocations and threats. If you continue down this path, I will not hesitate to take action to protect my people, and I will not be swayed by your empty boasts.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Why should I care about your people, Nikhil? They're just a bunch of tenants to me, not my responsibility.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be lectured to by a man who has consistently demonstrated a disregard for the well-being of our mutual tenantry, Sandip.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what exactly will you do, Nikhil, march into my estate with your little army of tenant peasants and try to take on the mighty Sandip?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I have no intention of marching into your estate, Sandip, but I will not stand idly by while you provoke a conflict that will bring harm to innocent people, including your own tenants.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what's this 'harm to innocent people' business? You're not suggesting I'm capable of intentionally harming my own tenants, are you?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I am suggesting exactly that, Sandip. Your actions have a direct impact on the lives of your tenants, and it is your duty as their landlord to ensure their well-being.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Oh, spare me the lecture on my duties, Nikhil. I'm well aware of what's good for my tenants, unlike some people who only care about lining their own pockets with gold.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not engage in a debate with you, Sandip, but I warn you again: your actions will have consequences, and I will not be responsible for them.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Nikhil, always the self-appointed guardian of the zamindar's conscience, but I think I'll manage to keep my tenants safe without your help.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Sandip, perhaps we should hear Nikhil out, rather than dismissing his concerns so readily.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: And what exactly do you propose I do, Nikhil? Arm my tenants with swords and shields to defend against the mighty Mussulman hordes?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your sarcasm, Sandip. I am warning you as a duty-bound zamindar, not as a favor to you. Take heed of my words, lest you regret it.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Come now, Nikhil, the mighty Mussulmans, how I tremble at the thought of their fierce attacks on my tranquil estate.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I say, Nikhil, don't you keep Browning among your books here? I was just telling Queen Bee of our college club. Do you remember that contest of ours over the translation of those lines from Browning? You don't?

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: I managed to get together the words to render it into Bengali, somehow, but the result was hardly likely to be a 'joy forever' to the people of Bengal. I really did think at one time that I was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence was kind enough to save me from that disaster. Do you remember old Dakshina? If he had not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet. I remember his rendering to this day ...

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: No, Queen Bee, it is no use rummaging those bookshelves. Nikhil has ceased to read poetry since his marriage--perhaps he has no further need for it. But I suppose 'the fever fit of poesy', as the Sanskrit has it, is about to attack me again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you a warning, Sandip

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: About the fever fit of poesy?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: For some time, Mahomedan preachers have been about stirring up the local Mussulmans. They are all wild with you, and may attack you any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Are you come to advise flight?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I have come to give you information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Had these estates been mine, such a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for me. If, instead of trying to frighten me, you give them a taste of your intimidation, that would be worthier both of you and me. Do you know that your weakness is weakening your neighbouring zamindars also?

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: I did not offer you my advice, Sandip. I wish you, too, would refrain from giving me yours. Besides, it is useless. And there is another thing I want to tell you. You and your followers have been secretly worrying and oppressing my tenantry. I cannot allow that any longer. So I must ask you to leave my territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: For fear of the Mussulmans, or is there any other fear you have to threaten me with?
